key_insight: PoreML provides a unified, physics-grounded pipeline for generating, training, and evaluating machine-learning models that predict multiphase flow in complex porous media.
engineering_relevance: The framework can accelerate design and screening for applications such as CO2 storage, fuel cells, and packaging by enabling more reliable pore-scale flow prediction.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible pore-scale data generation
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 time steps across synthetic and micro-CT-derived geometries
Unified evaluation for one-step prediction, autoregressive rollout, and transfer challenges
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation against analytical solutions and published experiments, plus domain-specific protocols to test predictive accuracy, physical consistency, and generalization across larger and real-material domains.
watch_item: Performance may still depend on data coverage and transferability, especially when moving from synthetic structures to micro-CT-derived porous media or larger domains.
paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
